messages:
nina: Quick monthly recurrence scan finished. Found three recurring themes we should assign: KV prefix evictions on long-context routes, slow model fallback after capacity spikes, and autoscaler warmup oscillation.

jordan: paste the filter you used?

nina: used `failures | group_by(signature) | count()` over 2026-01-01..2026-03-31. Sheet + graphs: https://redwood.company/ops/recur-2026-q1 (eng access). Top numbers: evictions +22% MoM on seq>2048, fallback p95 x2 in us-west-2, autoscaler flip correlated with node-image updates.

sam: Thanks. For the KV issue, is it cache TTL or shard sizing?

nina: TTL + eviction ordering. Also a quant-lib change increased per-key metadata, so working set grew. Not a leak.

lee: I'll pick KV mitigation. Plan: tighten prefix eviction policy, add mem-pressure alert, test larger KV shard in staging, measure hit-rate. Owner: lee. ETA: 2026-04-09.

anya: I'll help with alert and dashboard. Will add example alert rule and a dashboard panel.

jordan: For fallback slowness, repo shows two fallbacks during capacity events (2026-03-15, 03-19). Proposal: reduce routing health window for critical routes and evaluate a tiny warm pool for enterprise customers.

sam: i'll own routing changes (health window 30s->12s for high-priority routes). I'll draft an RFC with metrics and canary plan. ETA: 2026-04-16.

jordan: who can own warm pool infra?

ops-bot: @infra-leads flagged: warm-pool-capacity-review needed (auto).

incident-bot: tagging follow-ups into the PM board: https://redwood.company/pm/boards/incidents (automated).

lee: quick note on autoscaler oscillation: observed when burst_policy=enabled AND a node-image rollout happens concurrently. I think cooldown->30s isn't enough. Suggest adding a rollout-window lock to pause burst scaling during image updates. Owner: lee + infra. ETA: 2026-04-20.

jordan: ok let's put all three actions into the monthly ops cadence. I'll create a summary ticket linking the RFCs and assign owners. ETA: 2026-04-02 for ticket.

nina: thanks all. i'll re-run the recurrence scan after the changes and report next month.

sam: :thumbsup:
